title: Card Blocks and Replacement Cards — Card Operations Standard, Pocketwire Visa Debit Card
content:
**Standard.** A Pocketwire Visa Debit Card is blocked when the verified customer states that the card is lost, stolen or damaged, or that it has been used without their permission. The block reason recorded is lost, stolen, damaged or compromised to match. For this report, the customer's own statement is the authority. No record has to show the loss first.

The block takes effect immediately and is permanent. Authorization holds already placed on the card still settle or are released on their own schedule.

A replacement is issued at the customer's request, as a new card recorded as replacing the blocked card. Its fee follows the card's replacement charge rules. A blocked card with no replacement closes at its expiry month.

A card the customer simply cannot find at the moment is locked, not blocked.

### Statement to block reason

| The verified customer states the card is | Block reason recorded |
|---|---|
| lost | lost |
| stolen | stolen |
| damaged | damaged |
| used without their permission | compromised |
| not to be found at the moment, with no loss, theft, damage or misuse stated | no block: the card is locked instead |

### What a block covers

- A block applies to a card that is active, to a card that is locked, and to a card still ordered that the customer reports lost or stolen in the mail.
- A blocked card is closed once its replacement is activated. If no replacement was ordered, it is closed at its expiry month.
- The report is tied to the card the customer names, identified by that card's own record.

### Points of judgement (hypothetical)

- *"I think it's in my other jacket."* This customer cannot find the card at the moment and has not stated a loss, so the card is locked.
- *"There are purchases I never made."* The card has been used without permission. It is blocked with the reason compromised, immediately and permanently. A hotel hold placed before the block still settles or is released on its own schedule.
- *"My new card never came and I think it was taken from my mailbox."* The card is still ordered and is reported stolen in the mail, so it is blocked.
